nodes.summary: There is a natural number $B$ such that every finite $2$-group $G$ whose integral group ring $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ has the multiplicative Jordan decomposition property (MJD) but not the additive Jordan decomposition property (AJD) has order at most $B$. In particular, only finitely many isomorphism classes of finite $2$-groups have MJD but not AJD, which answers Kourovka Problem 16.104 in the affirmative.
nodes.title: Finitely many $2$-groups have MJD but not AJD

nodes.summary: An element $x$ of the monoid algebra $\mathbb{Q}[G]$ lies in $\mathbb{Z}[G]$ when all its coefficients are integers: for every $g \in G$, the coefficient of $x$ at $g$ is an integer.
